findings.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:56-90 — check-then-act TOCTOU: findFirst-then-create/update with no unique constraint or transaction means two concurrent webhook calls for the same userId+appId can both miss the findFirst and both insert, producing duplicate Credential rows for the same user/app (confidence 90, severity P0).

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:6-10 — `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` evaluate the zod builders' `.toString()` method at schema-definition time, producing the literal object keys `"ZodString"`/`"[object Object]"`-style strings (not a dynamic catchall), so the schema only requires `access_token` and silently accepts any other object shape as a "minimum" validated token response, defeating the intended validation of credential-sync payloads (confidence 90, severity P1).

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-16 — refreshOAuthTokens fetches CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with no timeout, retry cap, or circuit breaker, so a slow/unresponsive external sync endpoint blocks/fails the calendar/CRM refresh-token path for every integration wired to it, turning one external dependency into a single point of cascading failure across all refresh flows (confidence 70, severity P2).

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:66 — `appId: appMetadata.slug` stores the app's slug string into Credential.appId; this is consistent with createOAuthAppCredential.ts's existing convention (`appData.appId` is also the slug), so despite reading like a numeric-vs-slug mismatch, it is not a new inconsistency introduced by this diff (confidence 60, severity — advisory only, no defect).

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:59-63 — findFirst filters only by `userId` and `appId`, with no `teamId` scoping/guard, even though createOAuthAppCredential.ts treats team-owned credentials as a first-class case (state.teamId branch); a user-scoped webhook credential push could collide with or shadow team credentials sharing the same appId if a user also holds a team credential lookup elsewhere (confidence 40, severity P3, advisory).

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:1-93 — zero test coverage exists anywhere in the diff for the new webhook endpoint despite it having at least six distinct outcome paths (flag disabled, bad secret, bad body, user not found, app not found, decrypt+update, decrypt+create), so none of these acceptance paths are verified.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:1-23 and parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts — no unit tests were added for the new shared oauth utilities (refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse, createOAuthAppCredential, encodeOAuthState/decodeOAuthState) even though these are now load-bearing across six calendar/video/CRM integrations.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` is called with no try/catch, so a malformed body throws an uncaught ZodError instead of being handled as part of the endpoint's documented behavior, leaving that failure path unspecified/untested.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:58 — `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""` silently falls back to an empty-string encryption key with no startup/runtime validation that the key is configured, so a misconfigured deployment fails only when the first webhook call arrives (or worse, decrypts to garbage) rather than being caught as an explicit configuration requirement.

packages/app-store/zoho-bigin, tandemvideo, stripepayment (api/callback.ts changes) — these three apps were touched only to relocate encodeOAuthState/decodeOAuthState import paths, confirming they have no refresh_token flow; verified no other app-store integration with token-refresh logic (grep for refresh_token/refreshToken across packages/app-store) was left unconverted, so sibling-flag-propagation coverage of existing integrations is complete for this repo snapshot.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:12 — `import { throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam } from "../throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam"` resolves to `packages/app-store/_utils/throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam.ts`, a file that does not exist anywhere in the repo (confirmed via filesystem-wide search), so this module fails to compile. (confidence 100, severity P0)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:11 — `import { decodeOAuthState } from "../oauth/decodeOAuthState"` is written from inside `_utils/oauth/` itself, so it resolves to the non-existent `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts` instead of the sibling file `./decodeOAuthState.ts`, breaking the build. (confidence 100, severity P0)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` is called with no try/catch around it or the handler, so a malformed request body throws a ZodError uncaught by Next.js's default API handler, returning a raw 500 with a stack trace instead of a 4xx validation error. (confidence 90, P2)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:59 — `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` throws (e.g. "Unsupported state or unable to authenticate data" from Node crypto) when `keys` is garbled, the wrong key is configured, or the env var is unset/empty, and this is uncaught, producing a raw 500 instead of a 4xx. (confidence 85, P2)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:59 — `JSON.parse(...)` on the decrypted plaintext throws a SyntaxError uncaught if the decrypted payload isn't valid JSON (e.g. wrong key produces garbage that decrypts "successfully" under some cipher modes, or payload is empty), again surfacing as a raw 500. (confidence 75, P2)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:9 — `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, {...})` has no timeout/AbortController, so a hanging or slow-to-respond credential-sync endpoint stalls the calendar refresh path indefinitely with no bound on latency. (confidence 90, P2)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:16 — the function returns the raw fetch `Response` without checking `response.ok`/status, so a non-2xx response (e.g. 500 from the sync endpoint) is treated identically to success by callers. (confidence 90, P1)

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:86-91 — when `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a failed (non-ok) fetch Response, `res.data` is undefined because raw Response objects have no `.data` field, so `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;` throws an uncaught TypeError ("Cannot read properties of undefined") inside `refreshAccessToken`, crashing the calendar sync/refresh flow with a low-signal error instead of a clear "credential sync failed" message. (confidence 85, P1)

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:87 — `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError(...)` is an unreliable HTTP success check: many servers, proxies, and HTTP/2 responses return an empty or differently-cased statusText (e.g. "") even on a 200 OK response, so successful token refreshes can be misclassified as failures (false-positive throw), while checking statusText instead of `response.status`/`response.ok` also means actual non-2xx failures with statusText "OK" (unlikely but possible via proxies rewriting reason phrases) would be missed. (confidence 70, P2)

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:99-105 — `if (!accessTokenParsed.success) return Promise.reject(...)` is unreachable dead code: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:19-21) already throws synchronously when parsing fails, so its return value is always `{success: true, ...}`-shaped and never has `.success === false`, meaning this branch never executes and the actual failure path is the uncaught throw from parseRefreshTokenResponse. (confidence 70, P3)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:19-21 — `throw new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` is uncaught by any caller in the diff: googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts's `refreshAccessToken` inner try/catch wraps this call, but salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts's `authedApiClient`/connection-build path calls parseRefreshTokenResponse with no surrounding try/catch, so a bad refresh-token response crashes calendar operations with an unhandled rejection/uncaught throw rather than a handled credential-refresh failure. (confidence 60, P2)

packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17 — `const redirectUri = WEBAPP_URL + \`/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback\`;` replaces the dynamic `appConfig.slug` interpolation with a hardcoded literal, an unrelated regression bundled into an "OAuth credential sync" task with no stated requirement to change zoho-bigin's redirect-URI construction.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-100 — the new unconditional `fetch` token-refresh + `prisma.credential.update` runs on every `getSimpleAuthAttendee`/connection instantiation for every Salesforce user (not gated behind a credential-sharing opt-in flag or feature flag), changing existing Salesforce behavior for all users rather than being scoped to "add credential sync" as an additive/opt-in capability.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:1-53 — the salesforce change introduces a full token-refresh implementation (new zod schema, new fetch call, new util import `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) that duplicates/foreshadows generic OAuth-refresh infrastructure but is implemented ad hoc inside CalendarService rather than being traceable to any documented "credential sync" mechanism described in the task, suggesting the task description is too vague to confirm this is in-scope versus an unrelated hardening change.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:44-89 — `reqBody.userId` is an attacker-supplied integer accepted with only a shared-secret header check and no ownership/ACL verification, so anyone possessing (or brute-forcing) `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` can create or overwrite the OAuth/API credential for any user id in the instance (P0, confidence 100).

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:20-23 — the webhook secret comparison `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is a non-constant-time `!==` string compare, letting an attacker measure per-character timing differences to incrementally recover the shared secret (P2, confidence 50).

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:20-23 — if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset, `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is `undefined`; a request header value is always a string or `undefined` when absent, so an attacker omitting the header entirely makes `req.headers[headerName]` also `undefined`, and `undefined !== undefined` is false, causing the check to pass and fully open the endpoint with no secret configured (P0, confidence 75).

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:66-68 — decrypted `keys` JSON is written verbatim into `prisma.credential.key` for the target app without validating its shape against the app's expected credential schema, allowing an attacker who can produce a validly AES-encrypted (or, if the encryption key is misconfigured/empty, trivially self-encrypted) blob to inject arbitrary JSON into another user's stored credential object (P2, confidence 50).

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does a `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` and then conditionally `update` or `create`. This is a classic check-then-act sequence with no transaction/locking shown in the diff, so two concurrent webhook requests for the same `(userId, appId)` can both observe “no credential” and both execute `create`. Whether this results in duplicates depends on a DB-level unique constraint, but the diff does not show one, and the code itself is not concurrency-safe.
